questions.question_text: If sin (A − B) = 1/2 and cos (A + B) = 1/2, where 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, find A and B.
Prove that: (sin θ + cos θ)² + (sin θ − cos θ)² = 2
questions.model_answer:
(sin θ + cos θ)² = sin²θ + cos²θ + 2 sin θ cos θ and (sin θ − cos θ)² = sin²θ + cos²θ − 2 sin θ cos θ
Adding: 2(sin²θ + cos²θ)
= 2 × 1 = 2 = RHS (using sin²θ + cos²θ = 1)

points.expected: (sin θ + cos θ)² = sin²θ + cos²θ + 2 sin θ cos θ and (sin θ − cos θ)² = sin²θ + cos²θ − 2 sin θ cos θ

questions.question_text: Prove that: (sec A − tan A)² = (1 − sin A) / (1 + sin A)
questions.model_answer:
LHS = (1/cos A − sin A/cos A)²
= (1 − sin A)² / cos²A
cos²A = 1 − sin²A = (1 − sin A)(1 + sin A)
Cancelling (1 − sin A): = (1 − sin A)/(1 + sin A) = RHS

points.text: Applying identity cos²A = 1 − sin²A and factoring
points.expected: cos²A = 1 − sin²A = (1 − sin A)(1 + sin A)

questions.question_text: Prove that: cos A / (1 + sin A) + (1 + sin A) / cos A = 2 sec A
questions.model_answer:
LHS = [cos²A + (1 + sin A)²] / [cos A (1 + sin A)] (taking LCM)
Numerator = cos²A + 1 + 2 sin A + sin²A
= 1 + 1 + 2 sin A = 2(1 + sin A) (using sin²A + cos²A = 1)
= 2(1 + sin A) / [cos A (1 + sin A)] = 2/cos A
= 2 sec A = RHS

points.expected: LHS = [cos²A + (1 + sin A)²] / [cos A (1 + sin A)]

points.text: Using identity sin²A + cos²A = 1 and factoring

points.expected: = 2(1 + sin A) / [cos A (1 + sin A)] = 2/cos A

questions.question_text: A kite is flying at a height of 60 m above the ground. The string attached to the kite is tied to a point on the ground and makes an angle of 60° with the ground. Assuming there is no slack in the string, find the length of the string.
questions.model_answer:
Correct figure: right triangle, height 60 m, angle 60° at ground, string = hypotenuse L
sin 60° = 60 / L (perpendicular/hypotenuse)
√3/2 = 60/L ⇒ L = 120/√3
L = 40√3 m (≈ 69.28 m)

points.expected: Correct figure: right triangle, height 60 m, angle 60° at ground, string = hypotenuse L

questions.question_text: Prove that: tan θ / (1 − cot θ) + cot θ / (1 − tan θ) = 1 + sec θ cosec θ
questions.model_answer:
Writing cot θ = 1/tan θ: LHS = tan θ / (1 − 1/tan θ) + (1/tan θ) / (1 − tan θ)
= tan²θ/(tan θ − 1) − 1/[tan θ (tan θ − 1)] = (tan³θ − 1) / [tan θ (tan θ − 1)]
Using a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²): = (tan²θ + tan θ + 1) / tan θ
= tan θ + 1 + cot θ = 1 + (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1 + sec θ cosec θ = RHS

points.text: Expressing cot θ in terms of tan θ
points.expected: Writing cot θ = 1/tan θ: LHS = tan θ / (1 − 1/tan θ) + (1/tan θ) / (1 − tan θ)
= tan²θ/(tan θ − 1) − 1/[tan θ (tan θ − 1)] = (tan³θ − 1) / [tan θ (tan θ − 1)]
Using a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²): = (tan²θ + tan θ + 1) / tan θ

points.text: Splitting and converting to sin/cos to reach RHS

questions.question_text: From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Determine the height of the tower. (Take √3 = 1.732)
questions.model_answer:
Correct figure: building AB = 7 m, tower CD, BD = AE = x, angle of depression 45°, elevation 60°
In △ABD: tan 45° = AB/BD = 7/x ⇒ x = 7 m
In △AEC: tan 60° = CE/AE ⇒ CE = 7√3 m
Height of tower CD = CE + ED = 7√3 + 7 = 7(√3 + 1) ≈ 19.12 m

points.expected: Correct figure: building AB = 7 m, tower CD, BD = AE = x, angle of depression 45°, elevation 60°
Height of tower CD = CE + ED = 7√3 + 7 = 7(√3 + 1) ≈ 19.12 m

questions.question_text: Two poles of equal heights are standing opposite each other on either side of a road, which is 80 m wide. From a point between them on the road, the angles of elevation of the tops of the poles are 60° and 30° respectively. Find the height of the poles and the distances of the point from the poles.
questions.model_answer:
Correct figure: poles AB and CD, height h, point P on road, BP = x, PD = 80 − x
tan 60° = h/x ⇒ h = √3 x ; tan 30° = h/(80 − x) ⇒ h = (80 − x)/√3
√3 x = (80 − x)/√3 ⇒ 3x = 80 − x ⇒ x = 20 m
h = 20√3 m ≈ 34.64 m; distances from poles: 20 m and 60 m

points.expected: Correct figure: poles AB and CD, height h, point P on road, BP = x, PD = 80 − x

points.text: Forming trigonometric equations for both poles
